To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the tumor-specific antigen of adenovirus-12-induced tumor was found to be predominantly localized in the mitochondria and microsomes; 2) the fluorescent antibody method with the mitochondrial and microsome fractions as the antigens was applicable to the detection of the tumor antigen; and 3) the antigen was found to be present in the mitochondria of the normal hamster liver.

1) the use of the CF test for detecting antibodies to T-antigen of Adl2-induced tumor is useful in the detection of tumor-specific antigen in the cell fraction of Adl2-tumor, and 2) the predominant distribution of T-antigens in the microsomal and mitochondrial fractions of the tumor cells suggests that T-antigents are localized on the membranes of mitochondria and microsomes of the tumor cells.
the distribution of the tumor antigen in cell fraction of Ad12-induced tumors is different from those of the Ad12-infected hamster kidney cells.
